video.title: Facebook Founder Mark Zuckerberg Commencement Address | Harvard Commencement 2017

motivational.video_read: Mark Zuckerberg's 2017 Harvard commencement address. Most of it is commencement furniture — jokes, thank-yous, policy lists about UBI and climate — but there are three or four stretches where he speaks directly to the person who hasn't started yet: the fear of not knowing enough, the 'someone else will do it' excuse, being called crazy for ambition, and a story about a student with every reason to quit. That's where the material for the 2am scroller lives.

near_misses.why_not: 'I know too many people who didn't have a cushion to fall back on' is honest and names a real humiliation, but the message is 'success needs luck and money' — it removes self-blame yet leaves the viewer with no handhold. Direction check is shaky for this category.

The impostor confession — 'I wondered if I was just wrong, an impostor, a 22-year-old kid' — lands hard, but the resolution ('that is how things work when there's no sense of higher purpose') is about company-building, and the pain-to-turn ratio is off for a standalone reel.

The prayer he sings to his daughter and 'I hope you find the courage to make your life a blessing' is genuinely moving and heavily replayed, but it is comfort and blessing rather than a change in how the viewer sees themselves — likely the emotional finder's material.
The JFK janitor story and 'purpose is being part of something bigger than yourself' is well-made commencement material but the viewer's brain has filtered this sentence shape a thousand times.

skipped.what: cold open, applause, jokes about dropping out, the Facemash/Priscilla meet-cute — charming, not motivation
the 'three ways' roadmap and moon-shot history — list structure, no personal hit
climate, solar panels, curing disease, modernizing democracy — a project wish-list
wealth inequality, student loans, UBI, child care, charity stats — policy aimed at society, not at the viewer
the after-school entrepreneurship class and monthly dinners — warm giving-back anecdote, no turn for the viewer
global community, citizen of the world, the struggle of our time — geopolitics, not personal
shout-outs to graduating students (Agnes, Kayla, David) and local-community argument — needs the room's context

clips.title: No one knows how when they begin — ideas don't come out fully formed
clips.description: Zuckerberg dismantles the 'I don't know enough to start' excuse: 'Well, let me tell you a secret — no one does when they begin. Ideas don't come out fully formed; they only become clear as you work on them.' It lands on the payoff: 'If I had to know everything about connecting people before I got started, I never would have built Facebook.'

clips.title: Be prepared to be misunderstood
clips.description: A graduation-speech build that names what every big-vision person lives through — called crazy, blamed for not understanding it, criticised for moving too fast — and converts it: 'but that can't stop us from getting started.' The reel lands on that fuel-conversion line.
clips.boundary_note: Moved the end one word forward into L0099 because 'started' completes 'can't stop us from getting started' — the proposal's own closing phrase spans the line break. Dropped the opening 'okay' as throat-clearing; no question precedes this speech passage, so the thesis line itself is the correct start.

clips.title: Can I really do this? The student who had every reason to be cynical
clips.description: A commencement speaker voices the viewer's own doubt — "maybe you're asking yourself, can I really do this?" — then answers it with the story of his undocumented top student who, offered any birthday gift, asked only for "a book on social justice." It closes by handing the courage back to the viewer: if a high school senior with no certain future can do his part to move the world forward, "we owe it to the world to do our part too."
clips.boundary_note: Moved the start forward from the finder's 'it now' (a mid-sentence tail of 'create it now') to the sentence start 'maybe', so the clip opens on the question itself; kept the proposed close on 'we owe it to the world to do our part too'. The ~100s run is honest — question, story, and quotable close are each load-bearing with no dead air, and the 26.5s gap after confirms nothing trails.

segments.start_words: maybe you're asking yourself can I really do
segments.end_words: to the world to do our part too
segments.text: maybe you're asking yourself can I really do this well remember when I told you about that class I taught at the Boys and Girls Club one day after class I was talking to my students about going to college and one of my top students raised his hand and said that he wasn't sure he could go to college because he's undocumented Ed he wasn't sure if they'd take him last year I took him out to breakfast for his birthday and I wanted to get him a gift so I asked him what he wanted and he just started talking about struggles that he saw other students in his class facing and finally said you know I'd really just like a book on social justice I was blown away here is a young guy who has every reason to be cynical he wasn't sure if the country he calls home the only one he's known was going to deny him his dream of going to college but he wasn't feeling sorry for himself he wasn't even thinking of himself he has a greater sense of purpose and he's going to bring people along with him it says something about our situation today that I can't even say his name because I don't want to put him at risk but if a high school senior who doesn't know what the future holds for him can do his part to move the world forward then we owe it to the world to do our part too

clips.title: You're sure someone else is going to do it — but they're not. You will.
clips.description: Zuckerberg tells the Kirkland House founding story: he launched Facebook assuming one of the big tech companies would connect the whole world — it never occurred to him it might be them. It builds to the direct turn at the viewer: that change so clear you're sure someone else will make it? "But they're not, you will."
clips.boundary_note: Kept the proposal. Start is a clean sentence opening the story (a speech, no question to pull in); end stops mid-line on the payoff 'but they're not you will', excluding the pivot to the next topic ('but it's not enough to have that purpose yourself...').

segments.start_words: I remember that night I launched Facebook
segments.text: I remember that night I launched Facebook from that little dorm in Kirkland house I went to noes with my friend KX and I remember telling him clearly that I was excited to help connect the Harvard Community but one day someone would connect the whole world the thing is it never even occurred to me that that someone might be us we were just college kids we didn't know anything about that there were all these great big technology companies with all these resources and I just assumed one of them would do it but this idea was so clear to us that all people want to connect so we just kept working on it day after day after day and I know that a lot of you are going to have your own stories just like this a change in the world that seems so clear that you are sure someone else is going to do it but they're not you will
